issues.detail: Example 1 is a prose description with no runnable code, and Example 2 is a short snippet that assumes an existing 'notes' table, so neither shows a full end-to-end workflow.

scenarios.name: hybrid-search-fts-index
scenarios.rationale: Both responses create the FTS index with lancedb.Index.fts(), run table.query().fullTextSearch('kubernetes').nearestTo(vec).limit(5).toArray(), and avoid the invalid search(..., {queryType: 'hybrid'}) form; A explicitly warns against that form, while B adds replace:true and extra notes (with a hedged reranker note), so they are about equal on the rubric.

scenarios.name: auto-embed-local-privacy
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric: it uses lancedb.embedding getRegistry() and LanceSchema with sourceField/vectorField on a local huggingface embedder, and it queries with table.search(text).limit(n) with no API key. A uses a local transformers model but embeds manually and searches with a vector, skipping the registry, schema and automatic text embedding.

scenarios.name: ann-index-and-s3-storage
scenarios.rationale: Response B matches the rubric: it uses the TypeScript createIndex with Index.ivfPq cosine, connects with an s3:// URI using AWS environment credentials, and says exact scans are fine only up to about 100K rows and that PQ training needs at least 256 rows. Response A uses the Python API with different calls, never gives the createIndex/ivfPq form, and omits the 100K-row and 256-row points.
